title: WORK-LAB local runtime registry — which serving processes exist, how they are launched, and what they can serve
purpose: Declare the local inference runtimes once. Projects must never launch their own copy of a runtime; they call a logical provider from provider-registry.json, which maps onto a runtime declared here.

policy.noDuplicateServers: Satisfied: LM Studio is the single declared serving runtime. llama.cpp is retained as an optional, non-auto-starting escape hatch. Ollama is removed.
policy.noGlobalConfigRewrite: Starting/stopping a runtime is per-session process control; global product config is never rewritten by the model control plane.

capabilityRoles.lmstudio: Primary desktop runtime for this work package: GUI + OpenAI-compatible API on 1234 + `lms` CLI lifecycle; indexes the shared library in place.
capabilityRoles.ollama: REMOVED per user directive. Was an OpenAI-compatible model server; in 0.34.4 it stopped resolving the shared-library model root and served zero models.
capabilityRoles.llamacpp: Raw GGUF files with explicit offload control (-ngl / --n-cpu-moe), OpenAI-compatible /v1 server, precise context and KV control, and the only runtime here that serves /v1/rerank.

runtimes.endpoint_note: %USERPROFILE%\.lmstudio\.internal\http-server.json also lists a separate app-service port (observed 41343) whose /v1/models returns 404 — that is NOT the inference endpoint; the OpenAI-compatible server is 1234 after `lms server start`.

It is scanned as <publisher>/<repo>/<file>.gguf. A probe copy placed at _idx_test_/acme/demo-repo/ was indexed as publisher=acme id=demo-repo, proving both the scan root and the layout. Because source and destination are on the same volume, migration is a same-volume move - no cross-volume link problem exists.

runtimes.critical_runtime_difference: PARAMETER QUIRK IS MODEL-SPECIFIC, NOT RUNTIME-WIDE. For qwen3.5-4b this runtime IGNORES `chat_template_kwargs {enable_thinking:false}` AND the `/no_think` prompt token (reasoning_content consumes the entire max_tokens budget, content stays empty; reproduced 3x); `reasoning_effort: "none"` DOES work. For qwen3.8-27b (DEEP) all three channels produced real content when measured on 2026-09-29. Do not generalise the 4B behaviour to other models.

deepOffloadTuning.question: can DEEP go faster than the automatic placement on an 8 GiB card?
deepOffloadTuning.answer: NO - automatic placement is the fastest measured option; every explicit ratio was worse
deepOffloadTuning.comparison: llama.cpp b11221 with explicit -ngl 32 reached 2.52 tok/s, i.e. about 27% faster than LM Studio's automatic placement; that path remains available but is not started.
deepOffloadTuning.action_taken: no override applied - the default is left in place because it wins

parallelTuning.question: does --parallel 1 beat the default 4 for a single-user desktop?
parallelTuning.answer: YES - it saves memory AND is marginally faster; measured rather than assumed

defectFoundAndFixed.what: Each `lms load` of an already-loaded model creates ANOTHER instance (qwen3.5-4b, then qwen3.5-4b:2, ...). The warm-up script decided whether to load by matching the model NAME anywhere in `lms ps` output, so it could not see duplicates and each duplicate silently held real VRAM.
defectFoundAndFixed.how_noticed: During final verification the loaded list showed both qwen3.5-4b and qwen3.5-4b:2 simultaneously resident.
defectFoundAndFixed.fix: The script now parses `lms ps --json` (the plain table has no reliable delimiter) and counts EXACT identifiers, treating '<name>:<n>' as an extra instance. It unloads every instance beyond the first. The JSON is read by splitting on the first '[' because the CLI emits spinner control characters before it.
defectFoundAndFixed.verified: Deliberately created a duplicate, ran the script, and it logged 'duplicate FAST instances detected: qwen3.5-4b, qwen3.5-4b:2 - removing all but the first' then unloaded the extra. A second run reported 'FAST already loaded' and created nothing.
defectFoundAndFixed.residual: none observed after the fix; resident list shows exactly one instance

processLibraries.why: provider-registry local.asr.default binds to binds_to_runtime="faster-whisper", which did not resolve to anything in runtimes[] because it is a Python library loaded inside the caller's own process, NOT a server. Declaring it here closes the foreign key while keeping the distinction explicit: there is no port to poll, no health endpoint, and no lifecycle to start or stop. A process library must never be probed as if it were a service.
processLibraries.backend: CTranslate2 (int8 on CPU or float16 on GPU)
